candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care — staff education, competency support, and quality/safety improvement
candidate.educational_objective: Define just-in-time training as focused point-of-need reinforcement rather than a replacement for foundational competency.

options.A: It provides focused knowledge or skill reinforcement at the point of need, close to when the task will be performed.
options.B: It replaces foundational education and initial competency validation.
options.C: It is designed only for frequently performed routine tasks with no risk of skill decay.
options.D: It is useful only for expert clinicians and not for staff who need focused reinforcement.

candidate.rationale: AHRQ TeamSTEPPS describes just-in-time knowledge transfer as training at the point of need rather than 'just in case.' It is a reinforcement strategy and does not replace foundational education or competency requirements. A is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Just-in-time training transfers knowledge at the point of need rather than solely in advance 'just in case.'
candidate.source_locator: Why Is Coaching Important? — transfer of knowledge on a 'just-in-time' basis (training at the point of need)
candidate.source_organization: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ)
candidate.stem: Which statement best describes just-in-time training in clinical practice?
